Fit the property work around the production plan.

We organise maintenance of the premises around the way the site is used. Roof and cladding faults, doors, agreed lighting and plumbing, and external surfaces are identified separately from production equipment. Your site contact helps define access, interruptions and the sequence for each area.

01 / Plant and access on a roof

The building and the spaces around it

Map pedestrian and forklift routes at the boundary of building and production work. Agree access, separation and release by bay.

  • Roof, cladding and doors

    We scope leaks, visible building damage and door defects with attention to the work below or alongside the repair. Existing materials and fixing details are checked before replacement is defined.

  • Amenities and agreed services

    Plumbing, lighting and service-area maintenance is defined by the affected fixture or zone. Any interruption and restoration check is included in the plan.

  • Floors and outside routes

    We record external surface defects, drainage points and fixed access items alongside traffic, deliveries and material movement.

HVAC & building systems ↗

Specify for the existing building

Where the work meets a production area, identify which equipment and routes are controlled by the site team. Agree the scope and who confirms the affected section can return to use.

We check the surface, substrate, exposure and retained components before defining materials or repair extent. A visible floor or cladding defect can need investigation of the supporting condition before a local repair is finalised.

Installation height, work-zone availability, equipment access, waste and staged attendance influence the quote. We show investigation and additional findings separately rather than absorbing an unknown condition into a vague allowance.

Give us the property-side brief

  • Item and context

    Send the building area, problem history, photographs and any relevant material or equipment information.

  • Operating arrangements

    Include who controls access, routes that must remain available and any planned interruption window.

Hand back each work bay with clear boundaries.

We identify building items checked and conditions the operator must confirm before reopening the affected area.

Completion tied to the agreed zone

We document the building work completed and any follow-up decision. The handover keeps each repair connected to its location, avoiding confusion between property maintenance and separate production-equipment tasks.

Send photos and a site sketch, traffic routes, hot or noisy work restrictions, contact details and any required induction information.

We identify where building maintenance meets production equipment or a controlled work zone. The property brief records which work can happen beside normal operations, which area needs to be cleared and who confirms that production-side interfaces are ready.

  • Building scope and production boundary
  • Induction and restricted times
  • Area release responsibility

Common questions

Common questions

Does this include production machinery repairs?+

This page covers the agreed building, services and external-property work. We define that scope with your site contact and keep production-equipment requirements separate.

Can we group work into a planned shutdown?+

We can review the proposed list against the available window, materials and access. The agreed sequence identifies tasks that can be completed within that period and any necessary follow-up attendance.
